card.title: Kinetic friction
card.body: $f_k = \mu_k N$, directed opposite to the object's **sliding velocity** relative to the surface
card.says: once surfaces are **sliding** past each other, friction has a nearly constant magnitude $\mu_k N$—independent of sliding speed and contact area, and typically smaller than $f_{s,\max}$ ($\mu_k < \mu_s$).
card.from: empirical laws of dry sliding friction (Amontons and Coulomb), where $\mu_k$ (coefficient of kinetic friction) depends on the pair of contacting materials.
card.useWhen: an object is already sliding across a rough floor, table, or incline, and you need the friction force opposing its motion.
card.example: A $10\text{ kg}$ box slides on a flat floor ($g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2$, $N = 98\text{ N}$) with $\mu_k = 0.25$ → $f_k = 0.25 \times 98 = 24.5\text{ N}$ opposing motion. Pull forward with $44.5\text{ N}$ → $a = \dfrac{44.5 - 24.5}{10} = 2.0\text{ m/s}^2$.
card.analogy: Sliding a heavy sofa across a rug: once you break it loose, keeping it moving takes a steady, smaller push than starting it.
